checks: The unit sphere in one continuous dimension has isolated signs, so the local feasible chart varies only base coefficients and offsets. The stated positive- and negative-sign cap lengths hold for empty, proper and full intervals. In the two-sign cover problem the pointwise maximum is minimized by clipping the crossing to the interval, and the one-sign problems minimize at their appropriate endpoints.

A common finite closed polyhedral subdivision exists by refining all finite affine selections and signs. For a nonempty affine-cell feasible polyhedron, projection residual separation gives the nonnegative cone of active rows. Eliminating dependencies leaves independent rows with a uniform finite inverse bound over row subsets. This proves the residual estimate; incident cells all contain p_* and their extra inequalities are unviolated by the test point.

Every cap boundary has zero interval length, giving differentiability and continuity of the hinge gradient. A nearest feasible point remains in the local minimizer neighborhood by the error bound and continuity of violations. Therefore the positive-part penalty with finite coefficient has a local minimum while retaining the objective coefficient one.

The full-dimensional cells incident to p_* cover all short ray directions by their closures. Separation from the convex hull of their penalty gradients would give strict decrease along one such ray. Grouping the resulting convex combination only uses a constraint on cells where its penalty is active, yields nonnegative coefficients, and gives zero multipliers for inactive constraints.

Proper intervals contribute one counting point to the section derivative; empty slices contribute zero. Limiting endpoint patterns give correlated zero-one selections and their convex combinations use one shared density for all moments. Perturbing off the finitely many endpoint equations makes the unrestricted cap derivative ordinary, with unit normal factor one; the same limits therefore supply one consistent unrestricted generalized gradient rather than independent endpoint choices.

For a fixed dual weight vector the weighted interval minimum is affine in the free coefficients, with the stated gradient. At a differentiability point it touches the exact minimax maximum from below, hence its gradient agrees. Taking limits and convex combinations preserves dual optimality by compactness, continuity and concavity. The accepted zero-level saddle condition supplies one common actual contact.

Multiplying the continuous residual by u_i gives Psi_i after the mass and base balances cancel offsets and base terms at all positively weighted contact and section points. Since u_i²=1 this gives the displayed continuous equation. The proof uses no joint Fritz–John normalization theorem or strict feasibility.
The source hashes and exact locators cover the piecewise-affine error bound, penalty stationarity and lifted actual contact balances.

dependencies.hypotheses: Each closed interval is nonempty compact convex and has a finite affine margin family. Its attained primal and dual optima, exact cover sign and zero-level saddle/normal-cone condition give the needed actual contact. The error-bound and normal multiplier proof is independent of the joint Fritz–John theorem.

overlap.comparison: The general full-fiber theorem supplies an arbitrary Fritz–John multiplier, possibly with zero objective coefficient. The interval proof gives a normal choice at every local minimum.
The fixed-normal offset-only stress normalizes a reduced offset problem. It does not give simultaneous base-coefficient balances with one actual interval cap gradient and a shared contact.
The minimax lemma gives the primal-dual contact at zero cover margin, but has no multiplier existence or normalization claim.

readability: The opening phrase about objective multiplier one means existence of a normalized choice, as the rest of the statement and proof specify. It does not assert uniqueness of the multiplier system.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: A finite piecewise-affine error bound gives an exact penalty with objective coefficient one. Its gradient combinations yield actual interval section traces and optimal minimax contacts, and the continuous moment equation follows with the correct unit-sign convention.
